title: Normalized comparison on one supplied saturated tensor chart
statement: Let V,F,c,J be an fs log scheme with a characteristic fan chart and fan ideal. Let b:V' -> V be a saturated log blowup of c.pullbackIdeal J and assume its log structure is Zariski. Fix an affine-center input D [def-trf-fan-center-tensor-chart-data], a proof h of the prescribed stalkwise ideal generation equality, and a saturated LogIdealTensorCover C of D.idealChart h. For any saturated fan blowup beta:F' -> F along J and any a in D.generators, there exist an open K:S(R_a) -> F', a local map f from the actual restricted sharp space of the a tensor chart to S(R_a), and the normalized sharp-space map g induced by b. The map f followed by K has bijective stalk maps and its composite with beta equals the restricted g followed by c. At every geometric tensor-chart point, the fan stalk and the log characteristic are isomorphic to Associates(R_a localized at the face of monomials mapping to ring units). There is an ordinary-sharp-stalk/geometric-characteristic isomorphism e normalized on all ambient Zariski log sections. The two face-localization isomorphisms eF,eN take each canonical numerator q to its class represented by q, and e after the fan stalk map equals eN after eF on every stalk element. This is the single-chart comparison, conditional on b,h,C, and asserts none of their existence or the coherence of the center.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19--3.1.25, 3.3.12--3.3.13(i),(iii); parent proof steps 4--5 on one tensor chart.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monoid-chart-characteristic-fan] to the selected R_a tensor chart; C.isChart and C.chartAlpha identify its associated log structure with the ambient restriction. Transfer the sharp-space morphism and all normalized geometric stalk identifications across this open restriction. The ring-unit face is exactly logChartUnitFace(C.ringChart a).

By the saturated fan-blowup construction [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], the corresponding open chart of $F'$ is $S(R_a)$. Compose $c_{R_a}$ with its open inclusion into $F'$. Its composite to $S(P)\subset F$ and $c\circ b$ pull every canonical section $p\in P$ to the same characteristic section, namely the image of $h(p)$. The bijection of [lem-trf-affine-fan-hom-universal], applied to the sharp monoid $P$, proves equality of these two local morphisms, including their underlying continuous maps. Thus the constructed map is over $F$. At $w$, [lem-trf-monoid-chart-characteristic-fan] identifies its fan stalk and the geometric characteristic stalk with $(R_a)_{H_w}/H_w^{\mathrm{gp}}$, and already asserts the inverse-image sheaf isomorphism. Here $H_w$ is a face: a product in a local ring is a unit if and only if both factors are units. This gives exactly the stipulated $H_w$ and completes every local comparison. For any presentation of the supplied fan blowup, the a-chart is the locus where a generates the pulled-back ideal; the common localizations in P^gp identify these loci and their sheaves. The canonical map g is obtained from b.sectionMap by quotienting units and sheafifying. Transport the numerator formulas from the characteristic-fan theorem across K to obtain eF and eN; their equality with e on all fan-stalk elements follows because numerator classes generate the face localization modulo units.

proof_origin.place: ILO VIII 3.1.18--3.1.25, 3.3.4--3.3.13; formal decomposition of the supplied chart argument.
